title: Mini ethnographies: customer threads and tiny solution proposals
content:
Purpose: quick, human-centered snapshots from CS field calls -> short solution sketches we can test in a week. Goal is not to design full features but to surface patterns and tiny, testable changes that reduce customer pain or unlock clearer evidence for larger bets.

Method: pulled 8 calls (Apr 2026), annotated 12 follow-ups, 3 reproduce attempts in sandbox. Focus: latency surprises, model swap friction, billing confusion for embeddings, and retry/backoff behavior in burst scenarios.

---

1) Story: Retail analytics team (mid-market) — 'we lose reporters during spikes'
- Artifact: call w/ customer A on 2026-04-06; they run batched generation for nightly reports. Spikes when campaign descriptions are long -> serving runtime falls back to slower instance type (unannounced to them) and reports timeout.
- Observations (notes-to-self): customer notices timeouts, blames SDK. They tried toggling batch_size to 1 as workaround (painful). They cannot pin a model variant because of price pressure.
- Suggested tiny probes (1-week):
  - Expose a per-request header in SDK that surfaces "active instance tier" in debug logs (non-breaking) so CS can confirm fallback.
  - Add an opt-in server-side policy "prefer-latency-tier" that keeps requests on low-latency pool up to X tokens (configurable).
- Metrics to collect: #timeouts per customer per day, distribution of instance-tier changes in last-30-days, % of requests that changed model/variant mid-request.
- Possible ticket: JIRA CS-8241 (placeholder) to add logging header + telemetry spike.

2) Story: Fintech sandbox — 'embeddings cost math not intuitive'
- Artifact: email thread Apr 8; usage spike after they started embedding small documents for semantic search. They expected 1 embedding = 1 unit, confused by batching/padding.
- Observation: docs padded to fixed length by their client lib; they didn't realize tokenization changed cost. Billing view is per-embedding but per-token behind scenes.
- Tiny experiment:
  - Create an "Estimate embedding cost" quick-button in Console for a paste-in corpus (estimates based on tokenization + batching heuristics).
  - Small copy change in billing UI: add tooltip "embeddings billed by tokenized input length; batching and padding affect unit price" + example cases.
- Questions: can we compute estimate cheaply in-browser or must call backend? If backend, how to rate limit?

3) Story: Internal SaaS platform — 'rollout canary confused by model aliasing'
- Artifact: 3 customers reported that after a canary rollout, their app hit a new variant silently; rollback didn’t restore previous weights because alias mapping changed.
- Observation: users expect alias -> pinned version semantics; our routing policies are richer (region/capacity overrides) and not visible in rollout logs.
- Quick patch: add a 'rollout map' snapshot file per canary deployment that lists alias -> resolved model/version by region and capacity tier, downloadable from Console.
- Longer ask (parking): reconcile alias semantics in docs and plan a follow-up UI to show active routing policies.

4) Story: Platform ops (telecom) — 'unexpected token-limit enforcement on streaming responses'
- Artifact: support ticket Apr 14; a streaming response stopped mid-payload for a conversation with rapidly escalating role content. Customer built retry logic that expects stream resume; we truncated the stream and issued a generic error.
- Notes: we do hard enforcement on sequence length at router and on runtime kernel level. Need clearer error types and a resume token or hint.
- Tiny fixes:
  - Emit a distinct error code for 'stream-truncated-by-length' and include the truncated-prefix-length in debug logs.
  - SDK helper: provide a 'resume-from-prefix' helper that can reissue request with prefix cached.

---

Synthesis & patterns seen across threads:
- Visibility gap: customers want to see how the platform made routing/variant decisions (instance tier, region, overflow). Quick wins are logging/headers and downloadable snapshots rather than full UI redesign.
- Cost-mental models mismatch: billing views abstract units; customers reason about objects (1 doc -> 1 embedding). Small UI affordances (estimators, tooltips) reduce support load a lot.
- Short-circuitable problems: many field asks can be validated with "opt-in debug headers" + one-off console toggles. These are low-risk and accelerate evidence collection.
- Streaming & token enforcement are recurring friction points — consistent error codes and SDK helpers mitigate breakage while we design deeper runtime fixes.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Product: are we comfortable shipping server-side "prefer-latency-tier" as an account-level toggle? Who owns SLA/price messaging? (ops + pricing)
- Engineering: how intrusive is adding the debug header (runtime + SDK)? Estimate: 2-3 days infra + 1-2 days SDK/console.
- Billing: can we surface a cheap token-estimate endpoint? Ops concern: avoid heavy calls from Console. Alternative: run a sampled tokenization in-browser (open-source tokenizer wasm?)

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Maya: spin up CS reproduce for customer A (sandbox script + minimal trace) by 2026-04-24.
- Diego: scope debug header implementation, quick infra spike plan, PR template for logs — due 2026-04-28.
- Priya: draft billing estimator copy and mock console tooltip; check feasibility with frontend on tokenization options — due 2026-04-27.
- Evan: prototype SDK "resume-from-prefix" helper (typescript) and post to internal npm — due 2026-04-29.

Backlog (for later):
- Larger UX: interactive rollout map UI w/ region/tier filters (product + design).
- Runtime: more graceful streaming resume support (research kernel-level checkpointing).
- Billing: per-customer predicted spend alerts for atypical embedding usage.

Notes-to-self:
- Cite Slack thread #cs-field-threads (Apr 6-15) when passing notes to engineering; include raw transcripts for the infra spike.
- Keep all tiny experiments behind feature-flag or opt-in per-account to avoid accidental cost/latency regressions.

End: compact ethnography format — short story, observation, one-week probes, metrics, next-steps. If useful we can iterate this template and run a weekly 30-min "micro-probe" sync with Eng and Product to convert highest-value probes into spikes.

Raw snippets (cut-paste from calls) — keep for context: 
- "We thought a single embedding would be cheap, then our bill doubled after a single import" (customer B)
- "During lunch campaign, reports were fine; at 18:03 we saw a cascade of slowbacks and half our jobs timed out" (customer A)
- "Can we get an error that says ‘truncated for length’ and not something generic? My retry logic assumes idempotency" (customer C)
